title: grep
definition: Global Regular Expression Print. A powerful command-line utility used to search plain-text data sets for lines that match a regular expression or string.
simpleExplanation: The 'Ctrl+F' (Find) function for the terminal. You feed it a massive file, tell it what word to look for, and it spits out only the sentences containing that word.
realWorldExample: A user complains they can't log in. You type `grep 'username123' auth.log`. Grep scans the massive log file and prints out the exact single line showing 'username123 failed password authentication'.

basic: How do you make `grep` ignore case sensitivity (e.g., matching both 'Error' and 'error')?
intermediate: What happens when you pipe another command into grep, like `ls -l | grep 'Feb'`?

answers.question: Piping into grep?
answers.answer: Instead of searching a file, `grep` filters the live output of the `ls` command. It will only print the files that were modified in February, effectively filtering the list.

tableData.title: Important `grep` Command Flags
rows: Invert match. Shows every line that does NOT contain the word.
Recursive. Searches through all files in all subdirectories.
Count. Instead of printing the lines, it just prints the total number of matches.
Line number. Prints the exact line number where the match was found.
